title: Do not steal

lines: A SHORT MAN IN A SYCAMORE.
cards: Jericho, and a crowd lining the road. Zacchaeus is a chief tax collector, and rich, and too short to see over anyone, so he runs ahead and climbs a sycamore tree.
Jesus stops right under it, calls him by name, and invites himself to stay at his house. The crowd mutters about the company Jesus keeps.
And then Zacchaeus stands up and says: "Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold."

teach.b: "Thou shalt not steal." It sounds like a commandment about wallets and shoplifting. Scripture keeps pushing it further.
Leviticus says: "the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning." Sitting on a worker's pay is a kind of theft.
James is fiercer: "the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth." Withheld wages cry out.
So stealing can include the invoice you never quite pay, the hours you bill and don't work, the overtime you demand and don't pay for.

It can include time: the meeting that eats everyone's afternoon because nobody prepared. And it can include credit: your name on someone else's idea, a compliment you let land on you that belonged to a colleague.

Paul gives the cure in a sentence: "Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth." Notice the direction.
Not only stop taking. Start giving. That's what Zacchaeus does.

The story records no demand from Jesus and no lecture, only Jesus asking to stay at his house, and Zacchaeus offers to hand things back, four times over. Then Jesus says, "This day is salvation come to this house."
In this story, giving it back is part of what that day looks like.

how: Christian teaching on this commandment often extends it to fair wages, honest work and repaying what was taken, and some churches practice restitution as part of repentance, following the example of Zacchaeus.

games.why: "the half of my goods I give to the poor... I restore him fourfold." and Jesus says, "This day is salvation come to this house."

practice: Look back over the last week or month: whose idea did you use, whose work made yours look good, who covered for you or fixed the thing you got thanked for?
Let one name come up, and think how you'd say it out loud, in a meeting, an email, or straight to them. If you pray, you can give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Do not steal. Not taking what isn't yours, including wages, time and credit, and giving back what was taken.

orig.note: Hebrew: you shall not steal. The words of Exodus 20:15.
